newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia's Chiluba to name new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Zambia's Chiluba to name new cabinet.

text.p: Zambian President Frederick Chiluba has dissolved his cabinet and will appoint a new government from legislators who kept their seats in elections earlier this month, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"The president dissolved his cabinet on Wednesday, November 27," presidential spokesman Richard Sakala told Reuters.
He said there was no word on when the president would name a new team of ministers.

Chiluba and his ruling Movement to Multi-party Democracy (MMD) won a landslide in the November 18 elections and he had been under opposition pressure to scrap his cabinet after the dissolution of parliament a month ahead of the polls.
Law experts had said it was unconstitutional for the cabinet to stay in place after parliament was dissolved, but Chiluba insisted that the constitution allowed his government to remain for 90 days.

Chiluba was sworn in for a second term on November 21 after winning the elections, which were boycotted by seven opposition parties, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP).
Chiluba won with over 70 pecent of the vote, but final results from the controversial poll were not yet in 10 days after the ballot.
Kaunda was barred from taking part in the poll by a law excluding candidates with foreign parents. Kaunda's parents were Malawian.
